note: Thin lexical reference for the carrier-Ethernet VPN case. Identity-only entries. It has NO entry for proprietary/opaque items (x-mef-attr-5, vendor-evi-tag): those carry no public meaning and remain residual. The VLAN broadcast segment and the Ethernet Segment (ESI) are distinct entries, as are MAC-learning and MAC-mobility, so labels sharing 'segment' or 'MAC-' bind apart.

entries.label: Ethernet VPN service
entries.definition: The customer Ethernet service as one instance, whether described as a MEF EVC or an EVPN MAC-VRF.

entries.label: customer attachment
entries.definition: The interface where a customer site attaches to the carrier network for the service.

entries.label: service endpoint
entries.definition: The endpoint of the Ethernet service at one attachment.
entries.example: the service endpoint at the headquarters site

entries.label: customer VLAN broadcast domain
entries.definition: The customer VLAN carried by the service as one broadcast domain; a layer-2 forwarding domain, not a multi-homing link bundle.

entries.label: bandwidth profile
entries.definition: The ingress committed/excess rate policed at an attachment.

entries.label: class of service
entries.definition: The forwarding class applied to frames on the service.
entries.example: the real-time class mapped from PCP 5

entries.label: MAC learning
entries.definition: Learning customer source-MAC addresses at an attachment to build the forwarding table; distinct from handling a MAC that moves.
entries.example: dynamic learning at the headquarters attachment

entries.label: service MTU
entries.definition: The maximum service frame size carried end to end.

entries.label: service availability objective
entries.definition: The availability objective for the service; a service-view construct with no network-model counterpart.

entries.label: Ethernet Segment
entries.definition: The set of links by which a multi-homed site attaches to more than one PE, identified by an ESI; a multi-homing construct, not a VLAN.
entries.example: the dual-homed site's ESI on PE2 and PE3

entries.label: MAC mobility
entries.definition: The EVPN mechanism handling a customer MAC that moves between attachment points, using a sequence number; distinct from MAC learning.
entries.example: a sequence bump when a MAC moves from PE1 to PE2
